notes.text: Dispatch identity is committed in a separate transaction before the provider sees the request; a lost response becomes uncertain and is never retried.
Standing permission budget counts committed dispatching/uncertain/unresolved/succeeded ops as well as the used counter, so a rolled-back counter cannot overspend.
Only one unfinished connector mutation is allowed per task.

Global advisory lock 887832104 serializes stale-recovery/candidate selection; a per-connection advisory lock plus task and connection row locks are held across validation and the provider call so revocation waits for an admitted effect.
Slack post success requires ok+channel+ts in the receipt, otherwise the op is uncertain.
ProviderFailure.auth during read or dispatch marks the connection needs_reconnect, which also pauses event triggers using it.

features.title: Connected applications (Google, Slack, GitHub, MCP)
features.purpose: Let owner-selected bots read from and act on external accounts through a fixed action catalog, with exact owner review or scoped standing permission for every mutation, durable receipts and owner reconciliation of uncertain effects. Credentials never reach bots.

logic.step: Owner creates a connection (provider, bots, actions, per-action resource allow-list) and connects it via OAuth (Google/GitHub with PKCE; Slack OAuth only over HTTPS) or a private token; MCP uses a public HTTPS endpoint plus discovery
Bots discover allowed actions with hermbot_connectors (connections.accessible) and call hermbot_connector -> /internal/tools -> service.tool_action -> connections.invoke
invoke authorizes bot/action, resolves remembered references, validates arguments against the fixed catalog and resource policy
Reads execute immediately using a refreshed credential; results are redacted, references remembered, Drive imports saved to the library; auth failures mark needs_reconnect

Mutations: one unfinished per task; outcome bound; frozen payload; queued directly when an owner requested authorization or a standing permission matches, else an exact owner review (approval + pending operation)
Owner Allow once queues the op (connection revision recheck); deny settles outcome and resumes bot; edit supersedes the op and creates a new review

Task worker drive_one rechecks grant, policy, task state, revision, payload hash, approval/authorization/standing budget, commits dispatching marker, calls provider, records receipt and resumes the bot
Lost receipts (stale dispatching lease) become uncertain; owner reconciles with evidence; unresolved closure only after task stopped
Revocation: best-effort provider revoke, local credential removal, standing permissions revoked, event sources paused

flows.title: Connector action > review/approval > provider call > receipt/reconciliation
flows.summary: A bot calls hermbot_connector; reads run inline; mutations are frozen into a review (or matched to an owner request/standing permission), queued after Allow once, dispatched by the task worker with a committed dispatching marker, and settled with a definitive receipt or left uncertain for owner reconciliation.

steps.text: Bot tool hermbot_connector posts to /internal/tools; app.tools validates arguments and calls service.tool_action
tool_action resolves the connection and, for mutations, requires a work item; then calls connections.invoke
invoke authorizes bot/action, resolves remembered references, validates arguments against the fixed catalog and resource allow-list

Read: get credential (refresh if near expiry), call fixed provider endpoint via pinned transport, redact, remember references (or import Drive file to library); auth failure marks needs_reconnect and pauses event sources
Mutation: reject if task already has an unfinished op; resolve outcome; prepare_review freezes payload with connection revision and outcome revision
If an owner-requested authorization or a standing permission matches, insert a queued operation directly and set task waiting_approval
Otherwise service.request_review creates an approval (payload hash) and record_review inserts a pending connector_operations row
Attention trigger marks the task dirty; owner sees the review (flow:g)
Owner decides POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}: once -> op queued after connection revision recheck; deny/cancel -> denied, outcome settled, bot resumed. Edit (PUT) supersedes op and creates a new review
Task worker loop calls drive_one each iteration; under global advisory lock it marks stale dispatching ops uncertain and selects one queued op whose task has no active attempt

Under per-connection advisory lock, task lock and connection row lock, recheck grant, bot/action, task state/expiry, revision, resource, outcome state/dependencies, payload hash and approval/authorization/standing budget; failures finish as failed
Commit status dispatching with 120s lease in a separate transaction before the provider sees the request; increment standing permission use
Call MCP tools/call or the fixed provider adapter with operation-derived identifiers
finish_operation records succeeded/failed/uncertain, settles the outcome effect, emits connector.<status> and resumes the bot with a definitive receipt (uncertain does not resume)
Worker claim gate keeps a task with unfinished connector ops in waiting_approval
Owner reconciles uncertain ops in Connections > Activity (succeeded/failed with evidence, or unresolved after stopping) without replay
Successful receipts later feed own-write suppression for event triggers

flows.title: Routine tick > admission > run > history
flows.summary: Saved routine revisions bind a per-bot wake token; the task worker installs a Hermes no-agent 1-minute cron job in the bot runtime that posts a scoped wake; the API ticks due routines, admits idempotent occurrences into ordinary tasks; the worker first-claim gate rechecks; history derives status from work items.

steps.text: Owner saves routine via POST /api/v1/routines (app.py) or PUT /api/v1/routines/{id}; idempotent owner mutation; chat intake may save an inactive draft

Task worker runs routines.run; every 10s reconcile_schedulers computes wanted (any active routine) and PUTs generation/token/enabled to the bot runtime
runtime_api writes hermbot_routine_wakeup.py and hermbot-routine-wakeup.json {url, token}, creates/pauses/resumes the Hermes cron job "Hermbot wake <generation>" (every 1m, --no-agent)
Each minute Hermes runs the script, which POSTs {} with the bearer token to /internal/routine-wake/{bot}/{generation}
wake verifies generation and token hash, records last_tick_at and ticks if enabled
tick locks up to 50 due active routines for the bot (SKIP LOCKED); pauses after 3 definite failures or archived destination; records a gap row and applies catch-up latest after downtime

admit dedupes occurrence (and same scheduled_at across revisions), checks overlap, start window, daily cap and access; inserts admitted/skipped run with reason and frozen context (+since_success window)

admit creates a system thread message and, in a savepoint, create_saved_task: service.create_task (orchestration v2), budget, management bind, work_controller.apply requirements/effects; failure -> skipped
tick advances next_run_at (or state finished when none)
Worker claim_new locks the routine definition (SKIP LOCKED) and calls start_allowed which cancels if paused/archived/revised/destination archived/start window missed/access invalid
Execution proceeds as ordinary work (flow:a); pause_invalid in advance_waiters pauses definitions with invalid grants

flows.title: Event trigger (poll/socket/webhook) > trigger_worker > work
flows.summary: Events arrive by webhook ingress (API) or collectors in the event-worker (polls, Slack Socket Mode); each is durably deduped and matched to active trigger revisions in one transaction before acknowledgement; the event-worker admits ready pending runs into ordinary tasks via the shared saved-work path.

steps.text: Owner creates source, saves secrets, creates trigger (owner message revision, activated_at baseline for non-poll)
event-worker main loop (1s) claims poll sources (<=4 jobs, includes http) and socket sources (<=10) with 360s fenced leases
poll: credentials (connection refresh under row lock + source secrets), verify identity on initializing, http sources only heartbeat, fetch one page outside DB transaction
Drive: verify newly observed Google Docs against successful drive.create receipts with a read-only export
commit_page under lease: normalize items, ingest each, upsert resource versions, store cursor/progress atomically, schedule next poll, set activated_at on first complete baseline
socket: apps.connections.open, pinned wss connect, hello app_id, heartbeat extends lease; each envelope recorded via receive then acked after commit
webhook: POST /hooks/{provider}/{id} reads <=1 MiB in 10s, locks source, verifies signature with current/previous secret, handles Slack url_verification, receive(); response sent after commit
receive dedupes by delivery key/body hash, applies daily cap, normalizes (unsupported/recording_failed recorded), calls ingest and stores encrypted body only if recorded
ingest: event_key dedupe, availability check, own-write suppression, per active trigger match/baseline/access, insert event (encrypted if retained), delivery, pending/coalesced runs, matches

advance -> admit_pending: rotate, expire, lock conversation without waiting, overlap and per-bot queue checks, validate, self-event recheck (ignored), daily cap, wait for unsettled connector ops, then system thread + create_saved_task(origin=event) -> admitted
Worker claim_new: triggers.claim_locks then start_allowed with nonblocking share locks; cancels if revised/paused/expired/invalid

Failures classify source status, back off and pause triggers when access/resync/inspection needed; maintenance expires payloads/secrets and pauses unavailable destinations; heartbeat file for compose healthcheck

flows.title: Notification fan-out > web push > service worker
flows.summary: Domain row changes mark attention dirty via DB triggers; the notification-worker projects attention items and enqueues per-browser deliveries; a separate pump claims and sends generic VAPID Web Push through the pinned transport; the service worker shows a generic notification and routes clicks to the current attention resolution.

steps.text: Browser registration: Notifications.tsx registers /sw.js, PushManager.subscribe, POST /api/v1/notifications/subscriptions; server validates keys/endpoint, encrypts, sets device cookie and generation

delivery pump: claim under try-lock scans 30 due deliveries; suppresses irrelevant (eligible re-projects), reschedules quiet, folds batches into one summary (covered), defers bursts >=3/min, leases one as dispatching with TTL
deliver: live recheck, pywebpush with generic payload, Topic hash, VAPID claims, via PinnedSession -> connector_http.request
Record accepted/failed/expired/pending with backoff (lease-token fenced); 404/410 retire subscription, 401/403 server_key_error, accept updates subscription status

discrepancies.text: HTTP 401 and any non-rate-limited 403 are classified as auth failures, so an action-specific write-scope rejection marks the whole connection needs_reconnect (disabling still-valid reads and pausing event sources). Documented as open issue C37 deferred until baseline evaluations.

connector_oauth.finish failure path sets connections.status=needs_reconnect without a revision bump or triggers.connection_changed, unlike connections.needs_reconnect; dependent event sources are not marked needs_access and HTTP deliveries in that window are acknowledged but ignored (source_connection fails -> available=False).

Migration 006 tasks.connector_restricted (comment: keep connector admission restrictions across delegation) is now inert: native_policy always returns unrestricted and the flag is only projected. Documented Oct 11 policy change.
trigger_runs status CHECK allows 'failed' but no code writes it; failures leave runs pending with a reason or the task carries the failure.
Comment in GET /api/v1/event-sources says at most 100 archived sources are listed, but the query limits all sources to 200 (docs say archive listing bounded to 200 total).

Two routine systems coexist: legacy Phase 1 one-shot `routines` table/native Hermes job path (HERMBOT_ROUTINE prompt, dispatch_ticket) and Phase 5 routine_definitions. POST /api/v1/routines in app.py dispatches on body type (RoutineDefinition | RoutineRequest), so routine creation lives outside routines.routes().
A new event source saved with enabled=false is inserted with default status 'initializing' (not 'paused'); it is never claimed because claim requires enabled.
DELETE /api/v1/notifications/subscriptions/{id} returns {status: revoked} even when no row matches (no 404), unlike revoke_permission.
schema.sql is listed as containing notification/connector tables but contains none; connector tables are in 005.sql and notification tables in 017_attention.sql.

Webhook ingress returns distinct 404 messages for an unknown source id vs a provider/transport mismatch and takes the source row lock + decrypts secrets before signature verification; existence oracle and lock contention from unauthenticated callers (UUIDs are random, so low).
GitHub webhook signature covers the body only (no timestamp, delivery header unsigned); replay with a new X-GitHub-Delivery is only absorbed by event_key dedupe, as documented.
Gmail supplied Message-ID is replaced by Gmail (C40), so the reconciliation hint comment in the adapter overstates its usefulness.

workers.text: event-worker: separate compose service running backend.trigger_worker (read_only, tmpfs /tmp, 384m, 0.5 CPU, control net, depends on api healthy); healthcheck asserts /tmp/hermbot-events-heartbeat mtime < 30s; heartbeat touched after each ~1s pass
event-worker concurrency per process: up to 4 poll/http jobs (threads) and 10 Slack socket tasks; leases 360s fenced by lease_owner WORKER_ID + generation

notification-worker: separate compose service with two independent 0.5s pumps (projection, delivery); healthcheck on /tmp/hermbot-notifications-heartbeat (<30s); API exposes DB heartbeat_at (<30s) as worker_healthy because the file is container-local
Task worker hosts connector dispatch (drive_one once per loop iteration) and the routine scheduler reconciliation task (every 10s)
Routine timing source is a per-bot Hermes native cron job (every 1m, no-agent script) inside each bot runtime; the API wake endpoint performs tick

durability.text: Connector effects: dispatching marker committed in its own transaction before provider call; stale lease (120s) -> uncertain; never auto-replayed; owner reconcile records evidence

Event ingestion idempotency layers: trigger_deliveries PK (source, delivery_key) + body_hash, trigger_events UNIQUE (source, event_key), trigger_runs UNIQUE (trigger, occurrence_key), trigger_matches PK; HTTP/socket ack only after commit
Poll cursor/progress committed atomically with the events of that page under lease fence
Own-write suppression: Slack bot identity and successful connector receipts correlated to provider versions; rechecked at admission after receipts settle
Routine occurrences unique per (routine, occurrence_key); owner mutations idempotent through owner_receipts (registry.mutation)
Push deliveries unique per (subscription, generation, purpose); lease_token fences result writes; generations fence stale registrations
Event payloads retained encrypted 7 days; consumed identities kept forever to block old redelivery

concurrency.text: Advisory locks: 887832104 connector dispatcher; hashtextextended(connector:<id>) per connection; 887832115 source creation; 887832154 attention projection/notification claim (try-lock); 887832155 push registration; owner:<key> per idempotency key
Due-row selection uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (routine tick, trigger admission, source claim, invalid-grant pause) so multiple workers do not block each other
Admission takes destination conversation/connection share locks without waiting to avoid inverting archive/revocation lock order
Connector dispatch holds task row, connection row and per-connection advisory locks during the provider call (up to 20s per request; MCP several requests), so revocation waits for an admitted effect
Event collectors refresh OAuth credentials under the connection row lock; connector read path refreshes without that lock (possible concurrent refresh)

scaling-spof.text: Connector dispatch is globally serialized: one operation per worker iteration (~1s loop)
Push dispatch: claim returns at most one delivery per 0.5s cycle under a global try-lock shared with projection
Local caps: 100 live sources, 100 triggers/source, 10,000 deliveries/source/day, 200 listed routines, 10 browsers, 1000 pending deliveries/browser
Routines for a bot only tick while that bot runtime and its Hermes cron are running; machine/Docker must stay awake

security.text: Webhook auth: HMAC over raw body (GitHub sha256; Slack v0 with 300s timestamp; Standard Webhooks v1 with 300s timestamp), constant-time compare, optional previous-secret overlap, payload identity bound to stored Slack team/app and GitHub repository id; 1 MiB/10s body limit

OAuth: hashed one-use state, HttpOnly binding cookie scoped to callback path, initiating owner session check, connection/app revision fence, PKCE S256 (Google/GitHub), 10-minute expiry; callback page no-store with CSP default-src none
All credentials, event payloads, cursors, signing secrets, push subscriptions and wake tokens encrypted with Fernet CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY; hashes (sha256) used for lookup
Outbound requests use a pinned public address, no redirects or proxies, bounded size/time; MCP and push endpoints validated as public HTTPS
VAPID private key only in notification-worker environment; API has only public key/subject
Routine wake token is visible to the bot runtime (written into HERMES_HOME) but can only trigger a tick; it cannot supply instructions or grant access
External event text and connector results are labelled untrusted data; saved owner revision supplies instructions and authority

recovery.text: Source lease expiry lets another collector resume; socket shutdown records reconnecting + gap_since; failures back off exponentially (<=1h, honors Retry-After)
After downtime routines record one gap row and optionally admit only the latest occurrence within the start window
Expired notification leases are reclaimable; expired deliveries/subscriptions cleaned by maintenance

observability.text: db.event records connector.<status>, routine.*, trigger.*, trigger.source.error, notifications.preferences
Source health projected as disconnected when check-ins are stale; routine scheduler binding error/last_tick_at shown in routine list

control-vs-data-plane.text: Owner routes configure connections/routines/triggers/preferences (control); workers move data: task worker dispatches effects, event-worker collects/admits events, notification-worker projects/pushes

tradeoffs.decision: Native Hermes cron as wake signal rather than backend scheduler
tradeoffs.benefit: Uses supported Hermes mechanism; Hermes unmodified; wake cannot inject work
tradeoffs.cost: Depends on bot runtime availability and runtime adapter reconciliation

tradeoffs.decision: Polling/socket over webhooks for local deployment
tradeoffs.cost: Poll latency; intermediate changes may be missed

tradeoffs.benefit: No private data on lock screens or vendor servers; stale pushes harmless

unknowns.text: Exact frontend behavior of Connections/Routines/EventTriggers/Notifications beyond the API calls was not read (out of scope).
How tool_references.requested_authorization matches owner-requested authorizations (work_authorizations) was not read; only its call sites.
Hermes cron semantics (delivery guarantees, behavior while paused/after restart) are external to this repo.
